summary: Global markets are navigating a tense but cautiously stabilizing geopolitical environment, with sentiment modestly improving after Iran and Oman reached agreements on Strait of Hormuz access and revenue-sharing, easing immediate fears of a full energy supply blockade. The six-month-old US-Iran war remains the dominant macro driver, having disrupted Gulf shipping lanes, stranded Qatari gas exports, pushed British energy prices up 4%, and accelerated renewable energy investments across Europe and Asia, while the IMF's Georgieva acknowledges the global economy is weathering the energy shock but flags mounting fiscal risks. In equities, Boston Scientific shares are under pressure following a cyberattack disclosure, retail and software stocks face scrutiny over whether recent rallies reflect genuine fundamental improvement, and European energy and travel stocks have been hard hit, with Dubai's DXB airport reporting a greater than 30% drop in first-half passenger traffic. Investors are closely watching Iran-linked cybersecurity threats — including an FBI-scrutinized hack of a US water sector supplier — Hormuz shipping data still hovering below its 10-day average, oil company avoidance of Iran-blacklisted vessels, and the fate of Trump's Saudi nuclear deal tied to Israeli recognition. The short-term outlook hinges heavily on whether the Hormuz diplomatic accord holds and restores normal shipping volumes, with oil prices already dipping on tentative optimism, though persistent energy supply uncertainty and geopolitical fragility are likely to keep volatility elevated.
